"""Prepared window frames: named integer columns over a fixed row set.

The finite contract evaluates every predicate over the declared universe (and,
through universe indices, over the training records), so a frame is just the
per-cell value columns plus the slot families used by quantified projection.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any

try:  # optional vector backend; the pure-Python engine works without it
    import numpy as np
except Exception:  # pragma: no cover
    np = None  # type: ignore[assignment]


@dataclass(slots=True)
class PreparedDataset:
    name: str
    columns: tuple[str, ...]
    data: dict[str, np.ndarray]
    context_families: dict[str, list[str]]
    domains: dict[str, list[Any]]
    length: int
    metadata: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)

    def column(self, name: str) -> np.ndarray:
        return self.data[name]

    def family(self, name: str) -> list[str]:
        return self.context_families[name]


def cell_name(cell: int) -> str:
......
    domains = {
        cell_name(cell): universe.domain_of_cell(cell) for cell in range(universe.cell_count)
    }
    return PreparedDataset(
        name=name,
        columns=columns,
        data=data,
        context_families=families,
        domains=domains,
        length=int(universe.size),
        metadata={"source": "declared-domains", "cells": universe.cell_count},
    )


@dataclass(slots=True)
class ColumnFrame:
    """Dependency-free frame: plain Python integer columns over a fixed row set."""

    length: int
    data: dict[str, list[int]]
    context_families: dict[str, list[str]]


def columns_from_layout(layout: Any) -> ColumnFrame:
    """Materialise every universe cell as a periodic Python list column.

    Cell ``c`` repeats each domain value ``stride`` times and the whole block
    pattern repeats ``size // (stride * n)`` times, which is exactly the
    mixed-radix enumeration of the declared universe.
    """
    length = int(layout.size)
    data: dict[str, list[int]] = {}
    for cell in range(layout.cell_count):
        domain = layout.domain_of_cell(cell)
        stride = layout.stride_of_cell(cell)
        pattern: list[int] = []
        for value in domain:
            pattern.extend([value] * stride)
        repetitions = length // len(pattern)
        data[cell_name(cell)] = pattern * repetitions
    families = {
        name: [cell_name(slot * layout.field_count + index) for slot in range(layout.slots)]
        for index, name in enumerate(layout.field_names)
    }
    return ColumnFrame(length=length, data=data, context_families=families)
